Council Minutes  06/08/2020
   Councilmember Kennedy stated the following for the record:

  "Now is an extraordinary moment. A moment when the barbaric,
  chillingly, casual killing of George Floyd on a public street, closely
  followed the killing of Breanna Taylor in her own home during a
  botched execution of a no-knock warrant, the vigilante killing of
  jogger Ahmaud Arbery and the attempted weaponizing of the
  police by an entitled, rule-violating dog walker in New York City's
  Central Park, has belatedly created a national consensus that
  black lives do indeed matter. A moment when history will judge
  whether our core morality rose to confront the long-simmering
  racial justice issues as the world impatiently waits and watches. A
  moment that erases any disingenuous or conveniently oblivious
  claims of "I don't know" or "I am not aware." The question is can
  we meet this most extraordinary of moments?

  Pasadena is not immune or insulated from national movements or
  trends. We echo and mirror them. For many Pasadenans, the
  recent events in Minneapolis, Louisville, Georgia, and New York
  City triggered painful personal memories of their own experiences.

  To that point, I applaud the local protestors who have been
  peacefully exercising their most cherished of American rights. One
  event I must note is the protest organized by the Pasadena
  NAACP, clergy, Larry Campbell, and various community coalitions
  last Tuesday, June 2nd that began at First African Methodist
  Episcopal Church and caravanned to a program at City Hall where
  certain members of the Council, Mayor and others spoke. I was
  honored to participate in that historic, peaceful event.

  I also applaud the fine men and women of the Pasadena Police
  Department who have displayed calm professionalism and an
  understanding of this moment during the last 2 weeks and
  particularly during last week's protest. I must acknowledge Chief
  John Perez who set a welcome tone as he personally directed
  traffic for an extended period of time outside First AME Church at
  the start of the community vigil last Tuesday, June 2.

  Problems create opportunities. Opportunities to do better, to be
  better. Opportunities to genuinely ask where do we go from here?
  Can we meet this moment? In a glass half full spirit, I view this as
  a win-win opportunity. When everyone in our community is
  protected and served by the police, everyone, including the police,
  is safer. When the police are held to standards of justice similar to
  those imposed on residents, police are less likely to be vilified and
  endangered by those feeling aggrieved and vengeful.

  I offer 4 starting points, but admittedly not exhaustive, suggestions
  to move us forward and meet the moment: (1) Civilian Oversight,
  (2) Budget and Resource Review, (3) Interaction, and (4) Ongoing

Council Minutes  2  06/08/2020
   Review Process. We must impose self-discipline by establishing
  an ongoing review process to completely address what the heat
  of the moment may miss. In the warp speed of today that
  recognizes where our nation collectively was just 2 weeks ago
  today, before George Floyd became a household name and
  movement symbol, we must allow our decisions of the moment to
  have the flexibility to adapt to additional information and solutions.
  Our collective 5-second attention span cannot be allowed to
  undermine desperately needed justice as we soon move on to the
  next shiny object.

  We have an opportunity to be on the right side of history. Let's
  meet this moment and ensure that our actions match our words."

RECOMMENDATIONS FROM  COVID 19 UPDATE FROM CITY MANAGER:
OFFICERS AND
DEPARTMENTS  UPDATE ON HEALTH ORDER

  UPDATE ON RE-OPENING

  Steve Mermell, City Manager, provided introductory comments;
  and Dr. Ying Ying Goh, MD, Director of Public Health, provided an
  update and information on recent Health Orders and the City's
  efforts to re-open the local economy, continuance of requesting
  residents to stay Safe at Home, expectancy of the virus to spread,
  open sectors in the City, protocols developed by staff; and
  responded to questions. Manuel Carmona, Deputy Director of
  Public Health, provided information on staffs tracking of resilience
  readiness criteria, including state indicators to develop the City's
  COVID-19 Dashboard; and responded to questions.

  Vice Mayor Hampton stated that he does not believe that senior
  nursing facilities in Pasadena have been treated in the same way
  in terms of preventative measures, would like staff to develop an
  equivalent plan, and return to the City Council or the Public Safety
  Committee with an update.

  Councilmember Gordo stated that direct guidance is needed
  across various business sections in the City on re-opening
  procedures, and asked staff to seriously consider bolstering the
  number of employees who can go out in the field to provide such
  guidance. He stated that staff should proactively assist business
  in the re-opening process, direction/advice on how to comply with
  City Guidelines, and provide additional services as needed.

  Councilmember Wilson spoke on the need for additional staff to
  provide guidance to the various business sectors; and asked staff
  to send him information on the state indicators data that staff is
  tracking.

Council Minutes  3  06/08/2020

  COVID-19 pandemic, with lessons learned, missed opportunities,
  and areas that need improvement, City Manager Mermell stated

  and staffs response will occur, however currently staff and City

  suggested that the City Council and staff may consider hiring a

  members of the public advocating for fiscal assistance to local

  support of staff's proposals to re-open Pasadena businesses, and
  advocating to keep the Rose Bowl Loop and recreation area
  closed to vehicular traffic:

  Paul Little, Pasadena Chamber of Commerce
  Erika Foy, Pasadena resident
  Gene Wester, Pasadena resident

  Salvador Vasquez, South Pasadena resident
  Ben Planchon, Los Angeles resident
  Caroline Murrey, Pasadena resident
  Jon Burdett, Pasadena resident
  Matus Sobolic, Altadena resident
  Richard Garcia, Pasadena resident
  Daniel Lawlor, Pasadena resident
  Scott, Pasadena resident
  Howard Tan, residence not stated
  Chris Siraganian, Pasadena resident

  Richard Garcia, Pasadena resident

Council Minutes  4  06/08/2020
   RECOMMENDATION TO RESUME PARKING ENFORCEMENT
  EFFORTS
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Find that the proposed action is exempt from the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to State CEQA
  Guidelines Section 15061(b)(3) (Common Sense Exemption); and
  (2) Authorize the City Manager to resume regular parking
  enforcement efforts.

  City Manager Mermell provided introductory comments and Laura
  Cornejo, Director of Transportation and Jon Hamblen, Parking
  Manager, presented a PowerPoint presentation on the item, with
  all responding to questions.

  Councilmember Wilson expressed concern with resuming the
  enforcement of daytime street sweeping parking restrictions on
  June 22, 2020. He believes it is premature to commence the
  parking restrictions and many individuals are still working from
  home, and need to park their vehicles on the streets, and
  suggested that enforcement should resume on September 1,
  2020.

  Vice Mayor Hampton recommended a hybrid parking enforcement
  program in the business districts, including allowing free 20
  minutes parking spaces. He spoke in favor of extending the street
  sweeping parking restrictions to September 1, 2020; and allowing
  residents to purchase a temporary 6-month overnight parking
  permit.

  In response to Vice Mayor Hampton's request, Ms. Cornejo
  responded that staff will explore options to provide bi-annual and
  quarterly overnight parking permits; and staff is currently working
  on maintaining a select number of metered parking spots reserved
  for the suggested 20-minute timeframe to support curbside pickup
  and delivery services.

  Mayor Tomek spoke in favor of restoring the parking regulations
  with the exception of overnight parking and street sweeping
  enforcements, and agendize for further discussion those two items
  at a future Municipal Services Committee meeting.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Councilmember Wilson,
  seconded by Vice Mayor Hampton to approve the staff
  recommendation, amended to exclude daytime street sweeping
  enforcement and overnight parking enforcement until September
  1, 2020:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Gordo, Kennedy, Madison,
  Masuda, McAustin, Wilson, Vice Mayor Hampton,
  Mayor Tomek

Councilmember Gordo recused  ADOPTION OF GUIDELINES FOR THE EMERGENCY RENTAL
himself due to a potential  ASSISTANCE PROGRAM
conflict and left the meeting at  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council take
3:24 p.m.  the following actions:
  (1) Find that the proposed action is exempt from the California
  Environmental Quality Act ("CEQA") in accordance with State
  CEQA Guidelines Section 15061(b)(3), the "general rule" that
  CEQA only applies to projects that may have an effect on the
  environment;
  (2) Adopt the guidelines for the Emergency Rental Assistance
  Program (the "Program") as described in the agenda report; and
  (3) Authorize the City Manager to revise the adopted Program
  guidelines from time to time as may be necessary to implement
  the Program.

  William Huang, Director of Housing, provided introductory
  comments, and Randy Mabson, Program Coordinator II Manager,
  summarized the staff report as part of their oral presentation on
  the item; and responded to questions.

  Councilmember Kennedy spoke on the need for staff to ensure
  that the program captures the City's most vulnerable residents in
  the community, particularly seniors. He expressed concerns with
  the proposed ranked-based point system, specifically only
  providing 2 points for senior residents.

  Councilmember McAustin spoke on the need for the emergency
  rental assistance program to target and assist families in the City;
  and expressed concerns with the application process, which may
  be somewhat cumbersome. She asked staff to ensure that
  assistance (i.e. translation, uploading and printing documents) is
  made available to applicants; and to provide an update to the City
  Council in August of 2020.

  Councilmember Madison expressed concerns with providing
  senior residents additional points (additional opportunities) as
  many seniors live on their retirement income. He also expressed
  concerns with the tie-breaker No. 1 (reference to the census tract
  block) of the proposed guidelines, which he believes narrows the
  scope for the hardship criteria. Finally, he expressed concerns
  with the tie-breaker No. 3 (lottery determination) of the proposed
  guidelines, and suggested dividing up the available resources
  among all the qualified applicants.

Council Minutes  6  06/08/2020
   Vice Mayor Hampton expressed concerns with the limitations on
  applicants related to annual gross income, noting that the low-
  income thresholds may be too restrictive, however, he spoke in
  favor of the overall Emergency Rental Assistance Program.

  City Clerk Jomsky reported that 3 letters in support of the project
  and providing comments on the item were received, distributed to
  the City Council, posted on-line, and made part of the public
  record.

  He read aloud comments in support of the Emergency Rental
  Assistance Program from the following individuals:

  Leigh Ann Greenfield, Pasadena resident
  Roger Quintanilla, Pasadena resident
  Anthony Manousos, Pasadena resident
  Ruth McNevin, La Canada resident
  Jill Shook, Pasadena resident

  He read aloud comments expressing concerns with the
  Emergency Rental Assistance Program as lacking, among other
  things, rental forgiveness, from the following individuals:

  Matthew Sorrenti, Pasadena resident
  Ryan Bell, Pasadena resident
  Roger Quintanilla, Pasadena resident
  Allison Henry, Pasadena resident
  Natalia Govoni, Pasadena resident
  David Chavez, Pasadena resident

  Mayor Tomek stated that the City Council does not have the
  authority to impose rent forgiveness between property owners and
  tenants; and spoke in favor of the staff recommendation.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Councilmember McAustin,
  seconded by Councilmember Kennedy, to approve the staff
  recommendation:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Kennedy, Madison, Masuda,
  McAustin, Wilson, Vice Mayor Hampton, Mayor
  Tomek
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Councilmember Gordo
  ABSTAIN: None

  PERIOD OF JULY 1, 2020 TO JULY 1, 2023

Council Minutes  7  06/08/2020
   Recommendation of the Rose Bowl Operating Company: It is
  recommended that the City Council approve the following actions:
  (1) Find that the actions proposed in the agenda report are
  exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15061 (b )(3), the Common
  Sense Exemption;
  (2) Extend the Operating Agreement between the Rose Bowl
  Operating Company (RBOC) and the City of Pasadena from the
  current expiration date of July 1, 2020 to July 1, 2023 (latest date);
  and
  (3) Direct the parties to return to the Board and the City Council
  at least semi-annually with updates on progress concerning the
  RBOC's financial matters.

  Doug Kranwinkle, President of the Rose Bowl Operating
  Company, and Darryl Dunn, General Manager of the Rose Bowl
  Operating Company, presented a PowerPoint presentation on the
  item, and responded to questions.

  Mayor Tomek stated that the City Council should focus its
  discussion on the contract extension, as the Finance Committee
  will discuss additional issues and return to the City Council with a
  recommendation.

  Councilmember Madison reiterated his request that the staff
  reports include copies of the contract that is referenced in the
  agenda report; and spoke on the need to develop health safety
  guidelines and have those ready for deployment in the event that
  spectators will be allowed to attend sporting events at the Rose
  Bowl stadium.

  The City Council expressed appreciation and gratitude to Mr.
  Kranwinkle, Mr. Dunn and the Rose Bowl Operating Company
  Board and staff for their hard work during this challenging period.

  It was moved by Councilmember Kennedy, seconded by Vice
  Mayor Hampton, to approve the staff recommendation:

  AYES:  Councilmembers  Gordo,  Kennedy,  Madison,
  Masuda, McAustin, Wilson, Vice Mayor Hampton,
  Mayor Tomek
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

INFORMATION ITEM  RESULTS OF THE 2020 HOMELESS COUNT AND THE STATE
  OF HOMELESSNESS IN PASADENA
  Recommendation: This report is for information only; no City
  Council action is required.

Council Minutes  8  06/08/2020
   William Huang, Director of Housing, provided introductory
  comments, and Jennifer O'Reilly-Jones, Program Coordinator 11,
  presented a PowerPoint presentation on the item, and responded
  to questions.

  Councilmember Wilson asked staff to look at hotel/motels that
  show a willingness to accept homeless individuals in their
  facilities, to determine if there is an opportunity for long-term
  conversions.

  City Manager Mermell stated that he would provide an update on
  the faith-based community providing affordable housing on church
  properties and land use issues at a future City Council meeting.

  Vice Mayor Hampton suggested that staff consider offering
  waivers of Transient Occupancy Tax (TOT) fees to hotels/motels
  that allow homeless individuals to stay in hotels free of charge.

  Councilmember Gordo asked staff to provide comparative data
  and information on the Pasadena Outreach Response Team
  (PORT) and the Pasadena Police Department's Homeless
  Outreach Psychiatric Evaluation (HOPE) team to understand the
  effectiveness of both programs.

  Councilmember Kennedy spoke on the need to pursue
  partnerships with outside providers that have independent
  budgets and can provide supportive services to homeless
  individuals in Pasadena.

  The City Council expressed appreciation and gratitude to Mr.
  Huang, Jim Wong, Ms. O'Reilly-Jones, and the Housing
  Department staff for their excellent and hard work on the complex
  issue in assisting homeless individuals in the City.

  Mark Jomsky, City Clerk, read aloud comments advocating for
  additional resources to end homelessness, including various
  comments and suggestions related to rent control, additional
  renter protections, providing transitional and affordable housing,
  and expressing concerns with the number of transients in Arroyo
  Parkway area, from the following individuals:

  Sonja K. Berndt, Pasadena resident
  Teresa Eilers, South Pasadena resident
  Ferne Hayes, Pasadena resident
  Areta Crowell, Pasadena resident
  Anthony Manousos, Pasadena resident
  Erika Foy, Pasadena resident
  Jill Shook, Making Housing and Community Happen
  Allison Henry, Pasadena resident

Council Minutes  9  06/08/2020
   Councilmember Kennedy spoke on the need to revisit City-owned
  properties that might serve as locations for specialized housing to
  help eliminate homelessness in the City. He also spoke on the
  need to develop a marketing campaign to involve the community
  and seek their assistance in solving homelessness in the City,
  including building and offering Accessory Dwelling Units for rent.

  City Manager Mermell responded that there are two viable options
  and staff is in the process of advertising the availability of City-
  owned property adjacent to City Hall (commonly referred to the
  Water and Power site) and on Raymond Avenue (Rose Palace).
  He will meet with staff to discuss any other viable parcels.

  Vice Mayor Hampton asked staff to research empty buildings,
  including Pasadena Unified School District (PUSD) closed school
  sites, to convert into housing.

  Councilmember Gordo requested that in the future, staff distribute
  the complete housing report with the staff report, prior to the City
  Council meeting.

  Following discussion, by consensus of the City Council, and on
  order of the Mayor, the information was received and filed.

  On order of the Mayor, the regular meeting recessed at 5:53 p.m.
  to discuss the following closed session:

CLOSED SESSION  CONSIDERATION OF INITIATION OF LITIGATION pursuant to
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(4) (one potential case)

  The Mayor called the closed session to order at 5:54 p.m. (Absent:
  None):

  The above closed session item was discussed, with no reportable
  action at this time.

ADJOURNMENT  On order of the Mayor, the special meeting of the City Council
  adjourned at 6:22 p.m., in memory of all those that have lost their
  lives during the COVID-19 pandemic, and a moment of
  introspection for social justice and equity challenges the nation
  and the world faces as revealed by the killing of Mr. George Floyd.

  /s/ Terry Tornek
  Terry T ornek, Mayor
  City of Pasadena
